title: Epochal microphase timeboxing for tenant fairness and kernel hint propagation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We observe tail latency and unfair resource usage across multi-tenant hosts when prefill and decode phases interleave unpredictably. Current phase-splitting heuristics focus on token counts and immediate latency budgets, which can cause kernel thrashing and KV cache churn for tenants with bursty traffic. This ticket proposes a new allocation primitive, the 'epochal microphase timebox', which organizes prefill/decode work into short fixed-duration epochs to improve fairness, reduce kernel migrations, and allow kernel-selection hints to persist across microphases.
proposal: Introduce an epoch-based allocator that: 1) divides runtime scheduling into micro-epochs (configurable, e.g., 25-200ms) where a tenant or tenant-weighted cohort gets an exclusive soft timebox to produce prefill+decode work; 2) assigns kernel-selection hints (preferred kernel variant, quantized path, attention-sparsity hint) at epoch boundaries and bias runtime routing to respect hints for the epoch duration; 3) implements proportional epoch allocation based on tenant weight and SLA (latency-sensitive tenants get higher epoch frequency and hedging slots); 4) integrates a lightweight KV cache retention policy keyed by epoch ownership so cache amortization favors tenants with consecutive micro-epochs; 5) supports hedging within an epoch for latency SLOs by reserving a small instant slot to run speculative kernels on faster hardware when available.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduced kernel migration and KV cache churn, stronger temporal fairness guarantees, easier reasoning about per-tenant latency windows, and clearer knobs for latency vs throughput. Cons: fixed epochs can underutilize hardware when loads are sparse, added complexity to the arbiter, potential increase in queuing latency for very short requests waiting for the next epoch, and tuning required for epoch length and hedging budgets. This approach biases toward temporal fairness; absolute throughput optimality may decrease for certain burst patterns unless combined with opportunistic fill policies.
implementation_tasks: Design epoch allocator API and config (epoch_ms, hedging_fraction, tenant_weight_scale)
Add kernel-hint propagation: annotate requests at ingress and persist hint for epoch duration
Modify arbiter loop to schedule per-epoch ownership and enforce soft exclusivity
KV cache retention extension to honor epoch owners and implement fast eviction lane for demoted tenants
Hedging micro-slot executor: lightweight path to submit speculative kernels with time-limited cancel semantics
Unit + integration tests for epoch boundaries, hint propagation, and prefill/decode correctness
Benchmark harness runs across toy and production-like traces; add perf dashboards
Rollout plan automation: feature flag gated, canary on dev pool, then canary on 1% of hosts, then ramp
acceptance_criteria: No increase >5% in p50 latency for latency-sensitive tenants during 95th percentile load in bench traces
Reduction of kernel migration frequency by >=25% on mixed-tenant synthetic workload
KV cache hit-rate improvement >=10% for tenants with bursty sequences in bench traces
Observed proportional time allocation across tenants (measured by epoch ownership) within 3% of configured weights
End-to-end correctness: model outputs identical to baseline within numerical tolerance for gated models
Feature flag can disable without requiring runtime restarts and without leaving residual epoch state
monitoring: Add per-host and per-tenant metrics: epoch_count, epoch_owner_history(sampled), kernel_migrations_per_min, kv_cache_hit_by_epoch, hedged_invocations, epoch_idle_time_ms. Dashboards: epoch-allocator overview, tenant fairness heatmap, kernel-migration timeline. Alerts: sustained epoch_idle_time_ms > epoch_ms * 0.6, kernel_migrations spike +50% vs baseline, hedged_invocations error-rate >1%.
rollout: Gated behind 'epochal-timebox' feature flag. Start with internal dev cluster (canary A), run workload replay for 24h. If acceptance criteria hold, enable canary B on 1% production hosts for 48h with detailed metrics collection. Ramp to 10% then 50% over 2 weeks. Provide quick rollback to disable flag which drains current epoch owners gracefully.
open_questions: Optimal default epoch_ms for mixed workloads (start with 50ms? 100ms?)
How to blend epoch timeboxing with existing opportunistic batch fill — should fill be allowed to borrow across epoch boundaries?
Tenant weight calibration: how to infer weights from historical SLOs without manual config?
Interaction with Dedicated pools (reserved capacity): should epoching be disabled for dedicated GPUs?
Measurement overhead: how much sampling is safe for epoch_owner_history without adding overhead?
